implementation_summary: Converted 33 source rows (FR-1..FR-33) into 45 proposed requirements: REQ-001..REQ-033 map one-to-one to the FRs, and REQ-034..REQ-045 are split-off parts (robots.txt, rate limit, payment areas, mobile layout, accessibility and SEO basics, model per task, key encryption, no keys shipped, search data, free tiers, EN/TA handling, redesign vs repair), each tagged with its source FR. Priority mapped MVP=high, Phase 2=medium, Phase 3=low, with the original phase kept. Added a traceability table, glossary mappings, ADR constraints, security and privacy points, an indicative overlap table and 33 open questions with recommended defaults.
questions: Q-01: Is the source's audit-other-sites-to-pitch use case a new mode inside QA Flow Tester, a separate product on the same engine, or owner-side features only? Recommended: build the shared audit capabilities (FR-1 to FR-17, FR-20 to FR-22, FR-28) into the Check-up and hold FR-19, FR-23 to FR-25, FR-27, FR-31 and FR-33 until this is decided.
Q-02: What are 'the three audit documents' (FR-18)? Recommended: the three things FR-20 makes editable: page hierarchy, content and findings.

Q-03: Which external API gives page speed and Core Web Vitals, and what is 'search data' and where does it come from (FR-12)? Recommended: Google PageSpeed Insights API for speed; defer search data until a source is named, because Search Console needs the owner's access.

Q-04: Is the AI assessment (FR-16) a numeric score, a grade or written findings, and does 'ranking' mean search ranking? Recommended: written findings per area with evidence, no AI numeric score, kept out of any verdict; ranking means search ranking.

Q-05: Is FR-31 the price tool users pay (which conflicts with the recorded free tier plus monthly USD plans) or the price the tool user charges site owners, and what is the unit of '10'? Recommended: treat it as the tool user's service pricing shown in proposals and keep the recorded product pricing.
Q-07: Does a server-held product key for the first hosted check-up count as 'shipped' under FR-11? Recommended: no; 'no keys shipped' means no key in the repository, container image or wizard bundle.
risks: Crawling and storing content from third-party sites without the owner's consent (terms of service, server load); robots.txt and rate limits reduce the risk but do not remove it, and ADR 0015 pacing is undecided.

Unsolicited pitches to site owners (FR-19 opt-out wording): outreach rules vary by country, and opt-out text alone does not make outreach lawful; needs legal review, and the tool must never send the pitch itself.

Copyright: screenshots and extracted third-party content in the pitch, preview and documents; the FR-30 'no reuse of original wording' rule cannot be measured until defined, and AI rewrites can still be derivative or invent facts.
Login and payment area detection: a missed detection could let the crawler into a real checkout or account area on a third-party site; a false detection hides public pages.
Personal data: NAP of sole traders, staff names and the tool user's notes about owners are stored and sent to the AI Provider; retention and deletion are undefined.
Key encryption: ADR 0002 keeps a legacy .qa-keys.json fallback and the search found no encryption code in packages/, so FR-11 'keys stored encrypted' may not be met today.

Saved history and helper accounts on the hosted copy: ADR 0032 wipes /tmp, runs one instance and keeps sessions in memory, so persistent storage and user accounts add cost against the recorded $0 hosting direction.
Claim wording: pitch and owner documents invite persuasive claims ('insecure', 'not accessible') that ADR 0018 forbids.
Product positioning, pricing, hosting and key policy in the source conflict with the recorded direction (Q-01, Q-05, Q-06, Q-07).
Glossary collisions: 'Plan', 'project', 'sitemap' and 'account' in the source clash with CONTEXT.md terms; FR-26 needs a new name.
AI cost and free-tier quotas: a six-area AI assessment per page and external API daily quotas limit audit size and frequency.
Tamil, and later Hindi, in PDF and Word exports need embedded fonts; mixed Tamil and English pages complicate language detection.
handoff: All 45 requirements are proposed. Get the developer's answer to Q-01 (positioning) first: it decides whether REQ-019, REQ-023 to REQ-025, REQ-027, REQ-031 and REQ-033 stay in scope. Q-02, Q-03 and Q-04 block testable detail for the MVP requirements REQ-018, REQ-012, REQ-042 and REQ-016. Q-06 (hosting default) can take its recommended default (FR-29 already met by local plus Cloud Run). Copy the significant risks into engineering/risks.md. Before planning, have the repository analysis confirm the overlap table in requirements.md: it comes from targeted searches only, and FR-1, FR-8, FR-9, FR-13, FR-16, FR-18 to FR-20, FR-22 to FR-27 and FR-30 to FR-33 were not looked at. REQ-035 needs ADR 0015 accepted, and REQ-026 needs a CONTEXT.md term (Q-18).
